title: #618 Universal Toolchain Generator — Concept and Interface Specification
description: #618 Universal Toolchain Generator — Concept and Interface Specification. Part of the unified deeper project for #618, #617, #602, #735, #747.
body: This record is part of the unified deeper project combining the five priority tools from "Future Apex Simulators, Generators & Tools 601-750": #618 Universal Toolchain Generator, #617 Generator-of-Generators, #602 Simulator-of-Simulators, #735 Automatic Missing-Tool Detector, and #747 Evidence-Carrying Generator. The five are designed to work as one network: the detector finds what is missing, the generators build it, the simulators test it, and the evidence pack records the results. The Universal Toolchain Generator (#618) builds the connected programs required for a task rather than generating an isolated script. Given a task specification — goal, inputs, constraints — it emits a set of tool definitions plus a wiring manifest describing how data flows between them. Its interface contract requires every emitted tool to declare typed inputs, typed outputs, a run entry point, and a version, so the chain can be validated before anything executes. This record describes a PROPOSED capability, not a completed product. Nothing here claims the tool has been built, independently verified, or deployed. Design rule: a generated tool is NOT marked operational until it has a defined interface, a successful build, meaningful tests, and recorded results.

The five are designed to work as one network: the detector finds what is missing, the generators build it, the simulators test it, and the evidence pack records the results. The Automatic Missing-Tool Detector (#735) identifies a task blocked by unavailable capabilities and proposes the smallest set of new tools needed. Its specification defines a capability registry (which tools cover which capabilities), a task requirement list, a gap analyzer, and a set-cover proposer that minimizes the number — and cost — of new tools. It never proposes a tool the registry already covers. This record describes a PROPOSED capability, not a completed product.
